sovereign_country.strategic_role: 非洲第一大金融枢纽、辐射南部非洲关税同盟（SACU）商贸

business_scope.primary_industry_name: Online Sales of Maternity and Infant Care Commodities

meta_jurisdiction_context.legal_system_doctrine: Hybrid (Roman-Dutch civil law fused with English common law and customary law; constitutional supremacy)
applicable_bilateral_investment_treaties: European Union-South Africa Trade, Development and Cooperation Agreement (TDCA, 2004)
African Continental Free Trade Area (AfCFTA) Agreement (2019)
Income Tax Act 58 of 1962 s 108 Double Taxation Agreements (notably US, UK, Netherlands, China, India, Hong Kong SAR, Mauritius, Germany, France)

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Financial Intelligence Centre Act 38 of 2001 (FICA), as amended by the General Laws (Anti-Money Laundering and Combating Terrorism Financing) Amendment Act 22 of 2022 and FIC Directive 9 (2023); Companies Act 71 of 2008 s 50(3A)-(3B) and s 56, read with the Companies Regulations 2011 (as amended) and the Companies Amendment Act 16 of 2024 (commenced 27 December 2024); Protection of Constitutional Democracy against Terrorism and Related Activities Act 33 of 2004 (POCDATARA); Prevention of Organised Crime Act 121 of 1998. The national UBO register is maintained by the Companies and Intellectual Property Commission (CIPC); FICA CDD uses a 25% ownership/voting threshold while the Companies Act beneficial ownership register uses a 5% direct or indirect ownership or voting-rights threshold.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certified copy of each director's or shareholder's passport / national identity document
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Department of Home Affairs (Republic of South Africa) or foreign national issuing authority
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille (DIRCO) for foreign-origin documents; consular legalization only where the country of origin is not party to the 1961 Hague Apostille Convention

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Notarized beneficial ownership declaration affidavit (covering indirect control and interests of 5% or more)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notary public / Commissioner of Oaths in the country of residence
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille (DIRCO) if executed abroad; notarial certification if executed in South Africa; consular legalization for non-Hague contract states

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Police clearance certificate for each director and beneficial owner
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: SAPS Criminal Record Centre or equivalent foreign police authority
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille (DIRCO) or consular legalization for documents originating outside the Republic

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Proof of residential / business address (municipal account or bank statement dated within 3 months)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Municipality or registered bank (South African or foreign)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Notarized copy; Hague Apostille / consular legalization required only when the underlying document is issued outside South Africa

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of good standing / incorporation extract of any corporate shareholder
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Foreign companies registry (e.g., UK Companies House, Hong Kong Companies Registry)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille (DIRCO) or consular legalization where a non-Hague state; English translation accompanied by a translator's affidavit if not in English

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory PEP and sanctions screening of all promoters, directors, shareholders and UBOs against the OFAC SDN List, UN Security Council Consolidated List, EU Consolidated List, and the domestic terrorist listings maintained under ss 23-25 of POCDATARA; FICA s 28A requires accountable institutions (banks, notaries, company secretaries) to apply risk-based customer due diligence before the incorporation file is opened; enhanced due diligence and source-of-funds evidence are required where any person is a prominent influential person as defined in FICA and FIC Guidance Note 1 (2020); the low-risk standard e-commerce profile of the intended Pty Ltd permits standard CDD, but Stripe and PayPal will separately apply their own KYC onboarding for the South African merchant account.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Companies and Intellectual Property Commission (CIPC) Online Filing System (bizportal.cipc.co.za)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Names may be registered in any of the 11 official South African languages using Latin-script characters; English is the default CIPC processing language; there is no statutory transliteration requirement into English; the name must not be offensive, indecent, obscene, or falsely imply state patronage (Companies Act 71 of 2008, ss 11(2)(b) and 11(2)(c)).
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: Limited (permitted only where the entity is in fact a limited company)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: CIPC statutorily reserves a name for up to six months under Companies Regulations 2011 reg 13(1), but CIPC administrative practice grants a 20-business-day reservation; if the reservation lapses, file a fresh name reservation application (Form CoR 9.4). On rejection, the applicant may (i) file a new reservation with a distinctive element or with written consent from the holder of the conflicting name; (ii) apply for ministerial or sector-regulator approval where a sensitive token caused the rejection; or (iii) lodge a formal appeal with the Companies Tribunal under s 160 of the Companies Act by submitting Form CTR 160 within 20 business days after the CIPC rejection notice, requesting the Tribunal to direct CIPC to register the name.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Permissible for the online retail (e-commerce) model, provided a physical South African street address is used as the registered office at which mail is received and legal process can be served during business hours (Companies Act s 23(2)); a post box alone is prohibited; licensed virtual-office providers in Sandton, Rosebank, or Cape Town satisfy the requirement, and the registered address may differ from the principal trading address.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Low (approximately 5-8%) for a standard low-risk e-commerce importer-retailer; CIPC and the Financial Intelligence Centre conduct desk-based compliance reviews and targeted on-site inspections usually triggered by complaints, adverse media, unusual annual-return filings, or sector-related risk flags; physical inspection probability rises if SARS flags the merchant for VAT registration anomalies or if the Stripe/PayPal payment account is linked to third-party settlements.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: UBO register initial filing (submitted with incorporation application)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: No separate statutory fee charged where filed with the incorporation application

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Memorandum of Incorporation (MOI) drafting by legal practitioner
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing market benchmark for a standard single-class share MOI (ZAR 1,100)

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Professional incorporation administration (registered company secretary / CS practitioner)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing market benchmark for standard (Pty) Ltd incorporation including CoR forms and CIPC filing (ZAR 1,500)

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Registered office / virtual office setup (first three months)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing Sandton / Cape Town market benchmark (ZAR 550 per month)

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Notarial certification of director ID/passport and UBO affidavit
DIRCO apostille of foreign notarized documents and courier handling
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Department of International Relations and Cooperation (DIRCO)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Apostille issued free of charge; courier and agency handling benchmark (ZAR 380)

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Police clearance / PEP certificate for each director and UBO
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: SAPS Criminal Record Centre or foreign police authority
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: SAPS police clearance certificate statutory fee (ZAR 460)

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: AML / OFAC / UN sanctions database screening (all directors and UBOs)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Market benchmark for one-off PEP and sanctions batch query (ZAR 280)

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Companies Act 71 of 2008, as amended; sections 13, 14, 19, 40, 66 and 69; Companies Regulations, 2011.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Companies and Intellectual Property Commission (CIPC), South Africa
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Notice of Incorporation (Form CoR 15.1) filed together with the Memorandum of Incorporation (MOI)
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up capital is prescribed under the Companies Act 71 of 2008. No escrow account is legally required; upon allotment, the company must receive and record the agreed share consideration and maintain a securities register.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED that the allotment of 100 ordinary no-par value shares to the subscriber be ratified, and that the directors issue such shares upon receipt and recording of the agreed subscription consideration. RESOLVED FURTHER that the registered office of the company be and is hereby established at the address stated in the Notice of Incorporation, and that the chairperson be authorised to file the Notice with the Companies and Intellectual Property Commission. RESOLVED FURTHER that [Name] be and is hereby appointed as sole director, and [Name] as company secretary, each authorised to execute all ancillary incorporation and tax registration documents.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Reserve company name and conduct CIPC pre-registration search
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Log in to CIPC eServices, complete Form CoR 9.1 for name reservation, conduct a name search to avoid identical or confusingly similar marks, pay the reservation fee online, and retain the reservation certificate for submission with the Notice of Incorporation.
required_dossiers: Notarised power of attorney if using an agent
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If CIPC raises a name objection, file a revised CoR 9.1 with an alternative name or submit a formal explanation and consent letters; no substantive incorporation rights are lost.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Prepare Memorandum of Incorporation and ancillary consents
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Draft the MOI using the prescribed Companies Act provisions, insert the company name, registered office address, share structure, director powers and quorum. Complete the director consent forms and arrange notarisation where foreign signatories are involved.
required_dossiers: CoR 15.1A Consent to Act as Director signed by each first director
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the MOI is rejected for non-compliance, amend the affected clauses and resubmit via CIPC; no final incorporation rights are lost if corrected promptly.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: File statutory Notice of Incorporation with CIPC
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: CIPC eServices Portal, Company Registration Section
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the completed CoR 15.1 together with the MOI, name reservation certificate and director consents; pay the prescribed incorporation fee. CIPC verifies the documents and issues the registration certificate and company registration number generally within 2 to 5 business days.
required_dossiers: Director consent forms and certified IDs
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the filing is queried or rejected, use the CIPC correction process by re-uploading the defective schedule and paying the administrative correction fee; unresolved queries may be escalated to the CIPC contact centre using the assigned transaction reference.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Open corporate bank account and receive share subscription monies
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: A clearing bank licensed in South Africa (e.g. Standard Bank, FirstRand, Absa, Nedbank)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Lodge the CIPC registration certificate, MOI and certified director identities with the bank; complete FICA due diligence. Establish a dedicated company account to receive the share subscription contribution. No statutory escrow account is required, but bank internal account-opening rules apply.
required_dossiers: FICA declaration and source of funds information
Beneficial ownership information for bank KYC
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank asks for further information, supply a CIPC company extract dated within 90 days and clarify beneficial ownership; choose another bank if KYC conditions cannot be met.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Register for taxation and employment levies with SARS
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Register the company for corporate income tax on SARS eFiling; determine VAT registration based on the R1 million turnover threshold; register for PAYE, UIF and SDL once employees are engaged; nominate a public officer for tax purposes and obtain the relevant tax reference numbers.
required_dossiers: Director and public officer contact details
Registered office address and proof of business location
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If SARS issues a verification query, respond through eFiling within 21 business days with the requested supporting records; an extension may be requested in writing before the deadline.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Adopt statutory books and file beneficial ownership declaration
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Board of directors / CIPC Securities Register eServices
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Hold the first board meeting to approve the registered office, issue share certificates, open the securities register, adopt a minute book and complete the CIPC Beneficial Ownership filing using the company registration number. Keep a register of directors and prescribed officers.
required_dossiers: CIPC Beneficial Ownership form and supporting identity documents of ultimate beneficial owners
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the beneficial ownership filing is rejected, correct discrepancies in the ownership chain and resubmit; late filing penalties apply, so a notice of non-compliance should be addressed to CIPC promptly.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: National Regulator for Compulsory Specifications (NRCS), local municipal licensing authority, and Department of Employment and Labour where a physical warehouse, showroom or regulated baby goods imports are present
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: No general business licence is required for pure online resale; a municipal business licence or certificate of occupancy may be required for physical premises, and an NRCS Letter of Authority may apply to regulated baby goods such as cots, prams and car seats

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Department of Forestry, Fisheries and the Environment (DFFE)
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt from a full Environmental Impact Assessment for purely online retail and warehousing; a Basic Assessment screening may only be required if new storage floor area exceeds prescribed thresholds under NEMA EIA Listing Notices 1-3
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: No industrial discharge or VOC thresholds apply to pure e-commerce operations; any warehouse wash bay must comply with municipal sewer and trade effluent limits under the National Water Act, 1998 and applicable South African National Standards

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire safety certificate from the municipal Fire Services under the National Building Regulations and Building Standards Act 103 of 1977; electrical installation certificate of compliance; zoning and occupation certificate from the local municipality; and Occupational Health and Safety Act 85 of 1993 risk assessment for the workplace.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: South African Revenue Service (SARS) - eFiling portal (https://www.sarsefiling.co.za)
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: South African-incorporated (Pty) Ltd entities are automatically registered for income tax through the Companies and Intellectual Property Commission (CIPC) incorporation process and receive a permanent income tax reference number. A public officer who is ordinarily resident in South Africa must be appointed within 14 days of incorporation. Foreign resident vendors not incorporated in South Africa must register with SARS via eFiling using the RAV01 (Registration, Amendments and Verification) form to obtain an income tax reference number and must appoint a local representative taxpayer. VAT registration is applied for separately via eFiling using the VAT101 application; registration is compulsory once taxable supplies exceed ZAR 1,000,000 in any 12-consecutive-month period, or from the first rand for foreign suppliers of electronic services to South African recipients; voluntary VAT registration is available where annual taxable supplies exceed ZAR 50,000 and the applicant meets the stock or leasehold-enterprise conditions.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Entity_Level_Taxation; a (Pty) Ltd is a South African tax resident company taxed at the 27% corporate income tax rate on worldwide income (with foreign tax credits available), distributions attract 20% dividends tax (withholding), and capital gains are included in taxable income at the statutory corporate inclusion rate.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: South Africa does not operate a check-the-box pass-through election; a (Pty) Ltd is mandatorily taxed as a distinct entity. Available statutory elections include: VAT grouping election under section 50 of the Value-Added Tax Act; section 11D research and development allowance election; hybrid debt/equity instrument elections under sections 8E and 8EA; section 24I valuation-date and exchange-rate elections; section 23M interest-limiting elections; and elections relating to hybrid mismatch rules under sections 23N and 23O for cross-border structures.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Value-Added Tax (VAT) under the Value-Added Tax Act No. 89 of 1991
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: ZAR 1,000,000 (compulsory registration for taxable supplies made in any consecutive 12-month period); voluntary registration threshold: ZAR 50,000; foreign suppliers of electronic services: no threshold - mandatory from first rand of taxable supplies supplied to South African residents
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: South Africa does not yet mandate real-time fiscal clearance or digital stamping. SARS has announced a phased e-invoicing implementation roadmap with mandatory clearance expected progressively from 2026. Currently, electronic tax invoices are permitted provided they satisfy section 20 of the VAT Act (integrity, authenticity, readability, and prescribed content). Custom export declarations are lodged through the SACU electronic customs platform. Suppliers must retain copies of all tax invoices for five years per section 29 of the Tax Administration Act.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Under section 11(1)(a) of the VAT Act, the supply of movable goods qualifies for the 0% export rate if the supplier is satisfied that the goods will be physically exported from South Africa within 90 days of the date of supply, and the supplier retains the prescribed documentary proof of export. Supplies of services qualify for zero-rating under section 11(2), including services physically rendered outside South Africa (section 11(2)(a) read with section 11(2)(l)), international transport services, and services directly related to exported goods. The supplier must obtain and retain conclusive evidence-in-fact of export, including customs entry documentation and proof of foreign payment, before applying the zero rate.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (SAD500) with valid bill-of-entry number
Bill of Lading or Airway Bill evidencing physical removal from South Africa
Inward Remittance Certificate or bank statement proving receipt of foreign currency proceeds
Transport and freight documents (cargo insurance/weight certificates) substantiating the export journey
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: SARS audits export zero-rating claims under section 11, requiring retention of the full documentation pack for at least five years per the Tax Administration Act No. 28 of 2011 (s 29). Where documentary proof is inadequate, false, or the export did not occur within 90 days, SARS raises an additional VAT assessment clawing back the 15% output tax not accounted for. This triggers understatement penalties under section 222/223 of the Tax Administration Act, ranging from 10% (substantial understatement) to 150% (intentional tax evasion), plus statutory interest under section 187, and possible criminal prosecution for tax evasion under section 235, carrying imprisonment of up to five years. SARS may also disallow input VAT credits associated with the export supply and apply a 200% additional assessment in egregious fraud cases.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: Standard Bank of South Africa Limited

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: CIPC Annual Return (Companies Act Form CoR 30.1)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 30 business days after the anniversary date of incorporation; the deadline is tied to the company registration date, not the financial year-end.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late-filing penalty of approximately USD 10 per commenced month; repeated non-filing for two or more consecutive years may trigger CIPC delinquency proceedings and compulsory deregistration (strike-off).

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Corporate Income Tax Return (SARS Form ITR14)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 12 months after the end of the company's financial year; provisional tax payments (IRP6) are due at the end of the 6th month and at the end of the tax year.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: SARS levies an administrative penalty of 1% of the assessed tax per commenced month up to a maximum of 10%, plus understatement and interest charges; persistent non-filing may lead to an estimated assessment and enforcement collection against company assets.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Financial Statements (AFS) and applicable Audit or Independent Review Report
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Shareholders and board of directors; not publicly filed with CIPC for a non-public Proprietary Limited company unless required by its Memorandum of Incorporation or a court order.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: AFS must be prepared and presented to shareholders within 6 months after the financial year-end in accordance with the Companies Act 2008.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to prepare or present AFS is a statutory offence; directors may be held personally liable for losses caused by non-compliance, and CIPC may impose administrative fines or issue compliance notices.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: A Proprietary Limited company must obtain a statutory audit if its Public Interest Score (PIS) is 350 or more; if the PIS is between 100 and 349, an independent review by a registered accountant is required unless the Memorandum of Incorporation or shareholder resolution prescribes a full audit; if the PIS is below 100, no audit or review is required unless mandated by the company's founding documents or an applicable regulatory body.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: International Financial Reporting Standards (IFRS) for companies that are in the public interest or elect to use full IFRS; IFRS for SMEs is permitted for a non-public Proprietary Limited company; financial statements must be prepared in South African Rand.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: The annual return to CIPC requires confirmation of beneficial ownership details as recorded in the company's Beneficial Ownership Register. Any transfer of shares must be entered in the securities register and the Beneficial Ownership Register must be updated and filed with CIPC within 20 business days of the change; a verifiable copy of the updated register must be retained for CIPC inspection.

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 120–350 per annum for registered office/domicile address and CIPC filing support services in Johannesburg or Cape Town.
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 1,000–3,000 per annum for an independent review or full audit performed by a registered auditor for a small- to mid-sized e-commerce Proprietary Limited company.

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 27% (years of assessment ending on or after 31 March 2023; previously 28%)
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Section 11D R&D super-deduction (150%); Section 12E small business corporation rates for qualifying SMEs with turnover below R20 million; Section 12B renewable energy capex deduction (125%); Employment Tax Incentive for qualifying employees aged 18-29; no special retail/e-commerce incentive.
